classification.difficultyReason: Select the appropriate side ratio in each triangle; the hardest part simplifies x/x² to 1/x before solving for a positive length.

content.prompt: For each of the following, use a suitable trigonometric ratio to find the value of $x$, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Left vertical side 2, descending hypotenuse x, horizontal base, right angle at bottom left and 60-degree interior angle at bottom right. Ordinary marks use house black.
Horizontal hypotenuse at bottom, short left sloping leg x, upper descending leg 7, right angle at upper left and 20-degree interior angle at right. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: tan 20 degrees = x/7; the right-angle vertex is derived from perpendicular leg directions.

spec.description: Base x, unlabelled right vertical side, rising hypotenuse x squared, right angle at bottom right and 40-degree interior angle at bottom left. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: cos 40 degrees = x/x^2 = 1/x, with x positive because it is a side length.
